hook: Tomas Mikolov began experimenting with neural language models as a student in the Czech Republic in 2007, work that fed into his PhD at Brno University of Technology, completed in 2012, on recurrent neural network models of language. He joined Google as a research scientist and in 2013 published Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space with Kai Chen, Greg Corrado, and Jeffrey Dean, introducing the word2vec algorithm for learning dense vector representations of words from raw text. The technique made semantic relationships between words computable through simple vector arithmetic and was adopted across natural language processing almost overnight. Later that year he co-authored Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality, which introduced negative sampling and extended the method to phrases. He moved to Facebook AI Research in 2014, where he later contributed to the fastText library for efficient text classification and word representation across more than 150 languages. In 2019 he was named a Neuron Award laureate, and he has since led a research group at the CIIRC institute of the Czech Technical University in Prague.

achievements.title: Efficient Estimation of Word Representations in Vector Space (2013)
achievements.impact: Introduced word2vec, showing that simple neural models trained on large text corpora could produce word vectors that captured semantic and syntactic relationships, reshaping natural language processing practice.

achievements.title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality (2013)
achievements.impact: Introduced negative sampling and extended word2vec to phrases, making the method faster to train and more broadly useful.

achievements.title: fastText
achievements.impact: Contributed to a widely used open-source library for efficient text classification and word representation learning across many languages.

achievements.title: Neuron Award (2019)
achievements.impact: Recognized as a major scientific discovery in artificial intelligence and computer science.
